solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fish male clerk left out for cooking

indicators.note: something left out is omitted, so the word naming the side is dropped from the letters
cooking stirs ingredients together, so the remaining letters get mixed into a new order

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left; one L is removed

explanation.surface: A man working as a clerk is excluded from the kitchen while dinner is being prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Ls in MALE CLERK goes; the other eight letters rearrange to MACKEREL.
explanation.definitionFit: The mackerel is a common striped sea fish of the Atlantic, often eaten smoked.

clue.text: Encountered crook regularly in underground

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so only every other letter of the word is kept

explanation.surface: Someone bumped into a criminal on the Tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A metro is an underground railway system in a city, such as the Paris Métro.

clue.text: Photograph of the Spanish eleven initially plugging trophy

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
something plugging a hole sits inside it, so these letters go within the prize word

blocks.note: a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A picture of a Spanish football team clutching their trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a photograph taken at very short range, filling the frame with its subject.

clue.text: Deadpan European staying in one place

explanation.surface: A poker-faced continental who never moves from the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan delivery shows no feeling, which is what emotionless means: impassive and expressionless.

clue.text: Young bird, say, allowed around area

indicators.note: the short word for 'say' wraps around the letter that follows in the clue

explanation.surface: A fledgling, for instance, is permitted to roam the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual crossword signal for 'for example', abbreviated with two letters; 'around' applies only to that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An eaglet is a young eagle, a chick still in or near the nest.

clue.text: Employed, but taken advantage of

explanation.surface: A worker who has a job but feels exploited by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle covers both neutral utilisation and the unkind sense of being exploited by someone.

clue.text: Cut back on masonry initially dumped in builder's container

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is wanted
rubbish dumped in a receptacle ends up inside it, so this letter goes within the next word

blocks.note: a skip is a large open bin for building rubble

explanation.surface: Spending is trimmed as stonework goes in the rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British name for the big metal bin left outside building sites (a dumpster).
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp on something is to economise on it, spending or using less than is needed.

clue.text: Go off at a tangent about son in rented accommodation

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of items inside the word for lodgings

blocks.note: digs is British slang for lodgings

explanation.surface: A tenant rambles on about a son living in a rented flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Digs is British slang for rented rooms, usually a lodger's or student's.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject, which is exactly what going off at a tangent means.

clue.text: Complete yet difficult progress

blocks.note: rough going is hard, slow advance

explanation.surface: An arduous journey that has been finished despite obstacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete yet' looks like 'finished so far', but 'yet' means though, written THO.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoroughgoing means total or out-and-out, as in a thoroughgoing reform that leaves nothing untouched.

clue.text: Relative of Shakespearean fairy in more imposing surroundings

indicators.note: in, paired with the later word about surroundings, signals one piece sitting inside the other
surroundings enclose something, so the comparative wraps around the fairy

blocks.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A family member of a Shakespeare sprite lives in a grander house.
explanation.walkthrough: Moth, Peaseblossom, Cobweb and Mustardseed are the fairies attending Titania.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is a parent's mother, a close family relation.

clue.text: Daggers concealed in robe lining

indicators.note: concealed in says the letters lie tucked inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Knives are tucked away in the lining of a gown.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger-shaped printer's mark (†); obeli is its plural.

clue.text: Instance of former member overcome by drink

indicators.note: overcome by means engulfed, so the word for member is swallowed by the drink

explanation.surface: A case of an ex-MP who has had too much to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is one case or specimen of something, a synonym for an instance.

clue.text: A large tree growing in a mountainous region

blocks.note: standard abbreviation, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A big conifer thrives high up in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A large tree' reads as the subject; the definition is the whole phrase after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine plants are those native to high mountain slopes above the tree line.

clue.text: What broadcasters may use in traffic tailback, do we hear?

indicators.note: do we hear asks the solver to judge the phrase by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a line of cars is a queue of autos

explanation.surface: Newsreaders wonder whether they need a device while stuck in a traffic jam.
explanation.walkthrough: A tailback is the British word for a long line of stationary traffic. Autocue is the UK trade name for a teleprompter.
explanation.definitionFit: Presenters read their script from a screen beside the camera lens, the teleprompter known in Britain by this brand.

clue.text: Business transaction restricted by one's principles

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in, so the transaction sits within the other piece

blocks.note: one is I, with the possessive S
a deal is a business agreement

explanation.surface: A trader says their scruples limit which deals they can strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of conduct one aims at, the moral principles someone lives by.

clue.text: Try a casual worker in borders of Tibet

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters count
in places the casual worker between the two edge letters

explanation.surface: An invitation to try temping on the frontiers of Tibet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' stays outside at the front; only the worker sits between the borders.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort to do something, the noun sense of a try; both also work as verbs.

clue.text: Quick snooze set up worker in close-fitting headgear

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
in puts the turned-round worker inside the headgear

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker
a cap is a snug hat

explanation.surface: A labourer in a snug cap grabs forty winks.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short light sleep taken during the day, a brief doze.

clue.text: Girl taking a long time to produce a piece of mosaic

blocks.note: a girl's name, as in Tess of the d'Urbervilles
an era is a long period

explanation.surface: A young woman spends ages making a tile for a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles of stone or glass from which a mosaic is assembled.

clue.text: Do away with uncultivated vegetation

blocks.note: second meaning: stunted bushes and brushwood

explanation.surface: Get rid of the wild undergrowth.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel it, and scrub is also land covered with low scrubby bushes.

clue.text: Creature like Tarka having higher temperature in Bow?

indicators.note: Bow is an East End district whose Cockney speech drops the aitch at the start of words

explanation.surface: An otter runs a fever in the town of Bow.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in East London, Cockney territory, where the H is famously dropped. Tarka the Otter is Henry Williamson's 1927 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarka is the otter hero of a classic English animal story, so a creature like him is an otter.

clue.text: Posh doctor involved in Royal Academy dance

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the first two pieces go within the academy

explanation.surface: A smart physician takes part in a ball at the Royal Academy.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance with a rhythmic hip-swaying step.

clue.text: Flowering plant her many chums cultivated? About time

indicators.note: cultivated soil is worked over, so these letters are turned into a new order
About means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the unit of time

explanation.surface: A gardener's friends grew a bloom, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cultivated' suits a plant clue so well it reads as description, but it signals the rearrangement; the T goes inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysanthemum is a popular garden and florist's plant with large showy autumn blooms.

clue.text: Island easily located by Amundsen at first?

definitions.text: Island easily located by Amundsen at first?

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each preceding word

explanation.surface: A small Mediterranean island would pose no challenge to a great polar explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Roald Amundsen was the Norwegian who first reached the South Pole. The whole clue defines, and its tail supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was exiled, small enough for any explorer to find.

clue.text: Rate poet engineered for stage production

indicators.note: something engineered is constructed afresh, so these letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A versifier is graded on a piece written for the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera with spoken dialogue, performed on stage.
